1.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js is where LHError constructs its `friendlyMessage` and template ID, but it never invokes the i18n formatter when the error is thrown early.
• lighthouse-core/lib/i18n/i18n.js (and its companion locales files) define message templates (including `urlInvalid`), but the formatting functions aren’t hooked into LHError at instantiation.
• lighthouse-core/index.js is the entrypoint that validates the input URL and throws the raw LHError before any CLI-level locale swap or translation can occur.
• lighthouse-cli/run.js sets up flags, loads the core, and invokes Lighthouse, but it catches the error only after it’s already been thrown with an un-formatted template ID.
• lighthouse-cli/printer.js receives the caught error and prints `err.friendlyMessage` directly. Because friendlyMessage is still the un-formatted template ID, the CLI output shows the raw ICU key rather than a human-readable string.
1.bug_scenario: When you invoke the Lighthouse CLI with a URL that omits its protocol (e.g. `node lighthouse-cli www.example.com --view`), the tool throws an early, fatal LHError with code `INVALID_URL`. Because the i18n layer hasn’t yet formatted the error’s ICU template, you see the raw template ID (`lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js | urlInvalid # 0`) instead of a human-friendly, localized message (e.g. “Invalid URL: protocol is required”).

2.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js
  This is the class that creates LHError instances. Its constructor records the template ID (urlInvalid) but never invokes the message formatter here, so the friendlyMessage stays un-translated.

• lighthouse-core/lib/i18n/i18n.js
  The ICU message loader and formatter live here. Because no locale is swapped in or messages compiled before the fatal error, the raw template ID is all you ever see.

• lighthouse-core/index.js
  This is the core runner entrypoint. It throws the LHError synchronously (INVALID_URL) before calling swapLocale/loadLocale, so the i18n subsystem has never been initialized by the time the error is raised.

• lighthouse-cli/run.js
  This module is the CLI’s programmatic entrypoint (and what your reproduce script calls directly). It catches the LHError and prints err.friendlyMessage, but by then the message was never formatted. To fix the bug you need to ensure i18n.loadLocale (or swapLocale + message compilation) runs early—either in core/index.js or at the top of run.js—and/or invoke the formatter on the LHError before printing.
